subject.title: [Feature Request] SKILL.md Instruction Isolation from Agent Context

question: What trusted/untrusted authority boundary should OpenClaw enforce for SKILL.md content that is exposed through available skills or explicit skill invocation?
rationale: This choice defines public security semantics across prompt precedence, role authority, memory influence, tool grants, sandbox/profile behavior, and existing skill compatibility, so automation cannot safely infer it from the current visibility-only implementation.

options.title: Design Boundary First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the capability schema, enforcement points, compatibility behavior, and regression-proof requirements before implementation.

options.title: Land Partial Mitigations Separately
options.body: Allow scanner, manifest-visibility, or routing work to proceed as adjacent hardening while keeping this canonical isolation issue open until runtime enforcement exists.

options.title: Document Trusted Skills Assumption
options.body: Document installed skills as trusted model instructions and explicitly defer runtime isolation, accepting the residual security exposure for now.

recommendation.title: Design Boundary First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the capability schema, enforcement points, compatibility behavior, and regression-proof requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He is already active in this issue's security-boundary review and has the strongest recent prompt/skills routing history among the affected paths.
